issue_context.title: Clarify external CST signerName in docs and in CSR status fields
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->

**What happened**:

I spent some time helping a customer figure out they were misusing the recently added `signerName` field in a CSR.  They had been using CSRs for several releases to generate server certs for Kubernetes services that were only used within the cluster.  They found and read the Signers section of the [Certificate Signing article](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/certificate-signing-requests/#signers).  The predefined Kubernetes signers didn't seem to fit their use case so they made up their own `signerName`.  When they approved the CSRs no certs were issued; it looked much as if the CSR controller was failing or not even running.

It was an area I was unfamiliar with as well and it took a long time to realize the signerName they were using was the cause of the behavior and this was actually working correctly.

The PR that added this function has a sentence that makes the intent of the signerName field clear:

> Add 'signerName' field to the CertificateSigningRequest API to allow for external signers to be built

Some ideas coming out of this exercise:

Could the signer code add a condition or an event for the CSR resource indicating that the control plane is not issuing a certificate for an approved CSR because the signerName represents an external signer?

Could the documentation on [Signers](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/certificate-signing-requests/#signers) clarify that other names are allowed and that those are external signers and as such the control plane signer will not issue certificates - that is function the administrator must provide or install ?

For people who have been using the v1beta1 API, would it be appropriate for the "Kubernetes signers" section to suggest that CSRs for internal Kubernetes services "can use kubernetes.io/kubelet-serving as described in [Manage TLS Certificates in a Cluster](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tls/managing-tls-in-a-cluster/#create-a-certificate-signing-request)"

**What you expected to happen**:

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

- Create a CSR
- Send a CertificateSigningRequest resource to Kubernetes using:
```
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: my-svc.my-namespace
spec:
  request: $(cat server.csr | base64 | tr -d '\n')
  signerName: test.io/test
  usages:
  - digital signature
  - key encipherment
  - server auth
EOF
```
- Approve the CSR: `kubectl certificate approve my-svc.my-namespace`
- CSR is Approved but not Issued:
```
$ kubectl get csr my-svc.my-namespace
NAME                  AGE   SIGNERNAME     REQUESTOR                    CONDITION
my-svc.my-namespace   95m   test.io/test   c02pbtnd0d1gporb83jg-admin   Approved
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):  I've repeated this on 1.18 through 1.20.1
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:

> Could the signer code add a condition or an event for the CSR resource indicating that the control plane is not issuing a certificate for an approved CSR because the signerName represents an external signer?

I would not expect kubernetes signers to add conditions to CSR objects requesting different signers.

> Could the documentation on Signers clarify that other names are allowed and that those are external signers and as such the control plane signer will not issue certificates - that is function the administrator must provide or install ?

This sounds like a good idea to add to the signerName API documentation (in types.go) and to the website documentation at https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/certificate-signing-requests/

> For people who have been using the v1beta1 API, would it be appropriate for the "Kubernetes signers" section to suggest that CSRs for internal Kubernetes services "can use kubernetes.io/kubelet-serving as described in Manage TLS Certificates in a Cluster"

No, the `kubernetes.io/kubelet-serving` signerName is only intended for serving certificates issued to kubelets. I know @tallclair and @mikedanese (and maybe @deads2k) had interest in the "pod/service serving certificate" use case (xref https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/63732), but that would be implemented as a (new) distinct signerName.
